types.name: CodepointOffset
types.doc:
An offset between Unicode scalar values in a NativeKit document.

This is the coordinate system used by Skribidi and the editor transaction
protocol. It is deliberately distinct from UTF-8 bytes and UTF-16 units.

types.name: GraphemePosition
types.doc:
A code-point offset that has been aligned to a user-perceived grapheme
boundary. Grapheme positions use document coordinates, not cluster ordinals.

types.name: TextDocument
types.doc: Editable UTF-8 text with code-point, UTF-16, and paragraph indexes per segment.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: Incremented after each non-no-op replacement.

fields.name: editSince
fields.doc:
The replacement that turned revision `previous` into the current one, or null when that took more than one
replacement (or none). Lets a view of the document update only what the edit touched.

types.name: TextDocumentEdit
types.doc: One replacement, in code points: `[start, oldEnd)` of the previous text became `[start, newEnd)`.

fields.name: revision
fields.doc: The revision the replacement produced.

fields.name: previousCodepointCount
fields.doc: The document's length before the replacement.

types.name: TextOffsetMap
types.doc:
Cached coordinate conversions for one bounded UTF-8 segment. All conversion
methods use the coordinate name in their API so a
byte offset cannot be accidentally passed as a UTF-16 or code-point offset.

The generated grapheme boundaries cover the common Unicode rules needed by
editor movement (combining marks, emoji modifiers, ZWJ sequences, regional
indicator flags, Hangul, and Indic viramas). A shaping backend may replace
them with its authoritative boundaries using setGraphemeBoundaries().

fields.name: countCodepoints
fields.doc: Counts Unicode scalar values without retaining a second mapping cache.

fields.name: graphemePositionAt
fields.doc: Returns the nearest boundary, preferring the preceding one on a tie.

fields.name: previousGraphemeBoundary
fields.doc: Returns the preceding boundary, or the document start.

fields.name: nextGraphemeBoundary
fields.doc: Returns the following boundary, or the document end.

fields.name: graphemeBoundariesForRange
fields.doc:
Returns global grapheme boundaries within a code-point range as
subrange-local offsets. Both range edges are included so paragraph
views remain valid when a grapheme crosses a paragraph boundary.

fields.name: replaceCodepointsIncremental
paragraphRangeAt
fields.doc: Returns the paragraph containing a code-point position.

fields.name: paragraphCount
fields.doc: Returns the number of paragraph records, including empty paragraphs.

fields.name: paragraphIndexAtOffset
fields.doc: Returns the paragraph number containing a code-point offset.

fields.name: paragraphRangeAtIndex
fields.doc: Returns a paragraph range by its stable document-order number.

fields.name: setGraphemeBoundaries
fields.doc:
Replaces generated grapheme boundaries with shaping-engine boundaries.
Values are code-point offsets and must be sorted, unique, and inclusive of
both zero and codepointCount.

fields.name: replaceGraphemeBoundariesForRange
fields.doc: Replaces authoritative shaping boundaries for one document subrange.

types.name: TextRange
types.doc: A half-open Unicode code-point range in an editor document.

types.name: Utf16Offset
types.doc: An offset measured in UTF-16 code units, at a valid scalar boundary.

types.name: Utf8Offset
types.doc: An offset measured in UTF-8 bytes, always at a validated code-point boundary.

types.name: ViewportLight
types.doc: One light of a viewport's studio rig, in camera space.

fields.name: direction
fields.doc: Unit direction from the light into the scene, in camera space (x right, y up, z toward the viewer).

fields.name: intensity
fields.doc: Irradiance scale: a surface facing the light receives `intensity` times its albedo.

fields.name: color
fields.doc: Linear RGB tint.

fields.name: radius
fields.doc:
Angular radius of the light's soft panel, in radians. A panel is what metal reflects; zero makes the light a
point that only gives a specular highlight.

types.name: ViewportLook
types.doc:
The look of a 3D editor viewport, shared so that every view of a part reads the same: a light background
gradient, a workplane grid, and a studio rig of three lights that turns with the camera, with presets. A preset
is the whole lighting: lights, the room's sky and ground light, how strongly surfaces reflect the room, contact
obscurance, the roughness floor and the exposure. Edge lines contrast with their surface (`edgeColor`).

Colors are linear RGB triples and light directions are camera-space vectors, so this has no UI or renderer
dependency; each editor wraps them in its own color type and camera, and renderers outside the editor (the docs'
component viewers) build the same environment from these numbers.

fields.name: PresetNames
fields.doc: Preset names, indexed by preset, for settings and menus.

fields.name: SampleCount
fields.doc: Default multisample count for the scene image.

fields.name: GridStep
fields.doc: Default workplane grid spacing, in metres.

fields.name: EdgeContrastLuminance
fields.doc: Surfaces whose base colour has a linear luminance below this get `edgeOnDark` edges.

fields.name: lights
fields.doc: Key, fill and rim, in that order.

fields.name: sky
fields.doc: Room light from above and from below: the ambient term, and what surfaces reflect away from the lights.

fields.name: reflection
fields.doc: How strongly surfaces reflect the room, in [0, 1].

fields.name: occlusionRadius
fields.doc: Contact obscurance radius, in metres; zero disables it.

fields.name: occlusionStrength
fields.doc: Contact obscurance strength and angular bias, in [0, 1].

fields.name: roughnessFloor
fields.doc: Display-only minimum roughness, which broadens highlights on polished CAD faces.

fields.name: exposure
fields.doc: Exposure before tone mapping; zero shows shading clamped, without tone mapping.

fields.name: edgeOnLight
fields.doc: Edge lines on light surfaces: near black (display sRGB).

fields.name: edgeOnDark
fields.doc: Edge lines on dark surfaces (black oxide, rubber, dark paint): a light grey, so their edges stay readable.

fields.name: edgeColor
fields.doc: The edge colour for a surface of sRGB base colour `surface`.
